column1: # assets/genotype_rules.tsv: the genotype rules of step 42 (docs/42-traits.md#genotype-rules).
# A rule reads several sites together: the two haplotypes their genotypes make give one result.
# Hand-curated from the primary papers in the pmids column; no text is taken from SNPedia or any
# other database. GRCh38: ref is the GRCh38 base and alt the other allele the rule reads, both on
# the plus strand as in dbSNP's GRCh38 record, also for a gene on the minus strand.
# scripts/ci/check-rule-alleles.sh checks every site against dbSNP; bin/traits_report.py
# Four kinds of line, tab separated, each with its own columns:
#   rule         <rule> gene trait needs_phase ancestry note pmids
#   site         <rule> rsid chrom pos ref alt          (one per site, in the order the haplotypes use)
#   haplotype    <rule> name alleles                    (one base per site, comma separated)
# diplotypes: two haplotype names in the order of their haplotype lines, joined by /; when the
# genotypes allow several diplotypes, all of them in that order, joined by |.
# needs_phase yes: with two or more heterozygous sites the result needs to know which alleles sit
# on the same copy (WhatsHap, from the reads); without that the rule is unphased, not read.
# needs_phase no: the combination line is the one of every diplotype the genotypes allow.
# ancestry: yes when the reading depends on ancestry (the note says how).

column7: Odds ratios from a meta-analysis of people of European descent (Farrer 1997); the e4 effect was weaker in African American and Hispanic people and stronger in Japanese people. column4: Bitter taste haplotype (TAS2R38, PTC and PROP)
column7: The three TAS2R38 sites of the traits table read together: PAV (Pro49, Ala262, Val296) is the taster form and AVI (Ala49, Val262, Ile296) the non-taster form. Kim 2003 found five haplotypes worldwide; this rule reads the two common ones, and a copy with another (AAV, AAI, PVI or a rarer one) is not read. TAS2R38 lies on the minus strand, so the alleles here are the complement of the codon bases.

column5: Two copies of PAV, the taster form: in Bufe 2005 this group rated PTC and PROP the most bitter.

One PAV and one AVI copy: a taster. In Bufe 2005 this group recognised PTC and PROP as bitter at concentrations close to those of PAV/PAV; how bitter they rated them lay between the two homozygous groups and varied widely.
Two copies of AVI, the non-taster form: in Bufe 2005 the AVI receptor did not respond to PTC, and this group recognised PTC as bitter only at far higher concentrations. PROP responses varied more.
